topics.summary: Hallmarking certifies the proportion of gold in a jewellery article. Gold jewellery is graded under IS 1417 and assayed by the methods in IS 1418 at a BIS recognised Assaying and Hallmarking Centre.
details: Purity is expressed in carats and fineness, for example 22K916, 18K750 or 14K585.
The number after K is the parts of gold per thousand in the alloy.
The hallmark is applied by the recognised centre, not by the jeweller.
A hallmarked gold article carries the BIS standard mark, the purity grade and a HUID.

topics.summary: Silver jewellery and artefacts are graded for fineness under IS 15820 and carry the BIS standard mark together with the fineness grade.
details: Fineness grades apply to silver jewellery and artefacts.
Assaying and marking take place at a BIS recognised Assaying and Hallmarking Centre.
Marking requirements differ from those for gold; check the applicable grade for the article.

topics.summary: The HUID is a six-digit alphanumeric code assigned to each individual hallmarked article at the Assaying and Hallmarking Centre and recorded in the hallmarking database.
details: Each HUID is unique to one physical article.
The database records the jeweller, the centre, the purity and the article description against the code.
A consumer can enter the HUID in the official BIS verification facility to see the recorded details.
If the details shown do not match the article in hand, raise it with the seller and report it to BIS.

topics.summary: An independent facility recognised by BIS to assay precious metal articles and apply the hallmark. Recognition is granted for specified metals and test methods.
details: Fire assay by cupellation is the referee method for gold under IS 1418.
X-ray fluorescence is used for screening.
Centres are subject to periodic surveillance by BIS, including proficiency testing.
The centre applies the hallmark and records the article, including the HUID, in the database.

topics.topic: Consumer Verification of a Hallmarked Article
topics.summary: A consumer should check that the article carries all required marks, verify the HUID through the official BIS facility, and insist on an invoice recording the prescribed particulars.
details: Check for the BIS standard mark, the purity grade and the HUID on the article.
Verify the HUID in the official BIS verification facility.
Ask for an invoice showing net precious-metal weight, purity in carats and fineness, hallmarking charges and the HUID.
A consumer may get a hallmarked article re-tested at a recognised centre.
The hallmark certifies purity only - not weight, making charges, or the value of stones set in the article.

topics.summary: A jeweller registers with BIS through the hallmarking portal against each premises from which precious metal articles are sold, then gets articles hallmarked at a recognised centre before sale.
details: Register online and obtain the registration number.
Display the registration certificate at the place of business.
Send articles to a BIS recognised Assaying and Hallmarking Centre.
Sell only hallmarked articles where hallmarking is mandatory for that category and location.
Maintain records of articles sent for hallmarking and of articles sold.
